section: Direct tax reforms - income tax slabs, corporate tax cuts, faceless assessment, DTC debate
subsections: Direct Taxes Code and Income-tax Act 2025
Tax administration - PAN, faceless, AIS, TDS/TCS, Charter

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Draft Direct Taxes Code released
B. Direct Taxes Code Bill introduced
C. Direct Taxes Code Bill lapsed
D. Report of the new Direct Taxes Code task force headed by Akhilesh Ranjan
accepted.x: The draft Direct Taxes Code was released in 2009, the Bill was introduced in 2010, it lapsed in 2014, and the Akhilesh Ranjan task force submitted its report in 2019.
accepted.tq: Use the dated milestones and identify the first and last events before arranging the middle items.
accepted.sec: Direct Taxes Code and Income-tax Act 2025

accepted.s: Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, which one of the following replaces the concepts of the Assessment Year and the Previous Year?
accepted.x: The Act introduces a single 12-month ‘Tax Year’ beginning on 1 April, replacing the separate Assessment Year and Previous Year terminology.
accepted.tq: Test the exact statutory term and distinguish it from plausible but non-official alternatives.
accepted.sec: Direct Taxes Code and Income-tax Act 2025

accepted.s: A Permanent Account Number (PAN) is best described as a:
o: 10-digit numerical identifier issued by State Governments
12-digit numerical identifier issued only to companies
8-character alphabetic identifier used only for indirect taxes
accepted.x: PAN is a 10-character alphanumeric identifier used for tax and financial reporting purposes.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact length and alphanumeric format from numerical identifiers used elsewhere.
accepted.sec: Tax administration - PAN, faceless, AIS, TDS/TCS, Charter

accepted.s: In a PAN such as AFZPK 7190K, the fourth character ‘P’ indicates that the holder is a:
accepted.x: The fourth character of PAN indicates the holder type; ‘P’ denotes an individual, whereas ‘C’ denotes a company.
accepted.tq: Focus on the fourth-character code and distinguish the individual and company indicators.
accepted.sec: Tax administration - PAN, faceless, AIS, TDS/TCS, Charter

accepted.s:
With reference to tax administration reforms, consider the following statements:
1. Faceless assessment and the Taxpayers’ Charter were launched on 13 August 2020.
2. Faceless appeals were introduced in September 2020.
3. The initiative was associated with the expression ‘Transparent Taxation - Honouring the Honest’.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Faceless assessment and the Taxpayers’ Charter were launched on 13 August 2020, faceless appeals followed in September 2020, and the initiative used the stated expression.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the separate launch date, follow-up reform and official slogan.
accepted.sec: Tax administration - PAN, faceless, AIS, TDS/TCS, Charter

accepted.s: The Annual Information Statement (AIS) primarily:
o: Replaces PAN with a temporary transaction number
Contains only the taxpayer’s income-tax demand notices
Shows all reported transactions and widens the data available for pre-filled returns
Records only customs and GST transactions
accepted.x: AIS shows all reported transactions and, from 2021, widened the information earlier available through Form 26AS for pre-filled income-tax returns.
accepted.tq: Identify the functional purpose of the statement rather than confusing it with a demand notice or an indirect-tax record.
accepted.sec: Tax administration - PAN, faceless, AIS, TDS/TCS, Charter

accepted.s: Project Insight, launched in 2017 and made operational in 2019, is associated with:
o: Artificial intelligence and data analytics for tax compliance
Issuance of corporate bonds by SEBI
Digitisation of land records for State Governments
accepted.x: Project Insight uses artificial intelligence and data analytics to improve tax compliance.
accepted.tq: Match the named project with its specific technology and administrative objective.
accepted.sec: Tax administration - PAN, faceless, AIS, TDS/TCS, Charter

accepted.s: Under the Budget 2026-27 measure concerning Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) remittances for education and medical purposes, the rate of Tax Collected at Source (TCS) was proposed to be reduced from:
accepted.x: The TCS rate on LRS remittances for education and medical purposes was reduced from 5 per cent to 2 per cent.
accepted.tq: Read the rate movement in the correct direction and distinguish the old rate from the new rate.
accepted.sec: Tax administration - PAN, faceless, AIS, TDS/TCS, Charter

accepted.s: A resident purchasing property from a non-resident, under the Budget 2026-27 provision, may deduct TDS using:
accepted.x: The provision allows resident buyers of property from non-residents to deduct TDS using PAN instead of TAN.
accepted.tq: Separate the two commonly confused tax identifiers by asking which one substitutes for the other.
accepted.sec: Tax administration - PAN, faceless, AIS, TDS/TCS, Charter

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the change relating to ICDS and Ind AS?
o: Ind AS is to be merged into ICDS, and separate Ind AS accounting is to be dropped from tax year 2026-27.
ICDS is to be converted into GST accounting from tax year 2025-26.
ICDS is to be merged into Ind AS, and separate ICDS accounting is to be dropped from tax year 2027-28.
Both ICDS and Ind AS are to be abolished from tax year 2027-28.
accepted.x: The proposed change merges ICDS into Ind AS and drops separate ICDS accounting from tax year 2027-28.
accepted.tq: Watch the direction of the merger and the specific commencement tax year.
accepted.sec: Tax administration - PAN, faceless, AIS, TDS/TCS, Charter

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT):
1. It is the apex body for direct taxes.
2. It functions as a statutory body under the Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963.
3. It is placed in the Department of Revenue.
4. It is the cadre controller of the Indian Revenue Service.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. CBDT is the statutory apex direct-tax body under the Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963, located in the Department of Revenue and serving as cadre controller of the IRS.
accepted.tq: Verify the body’s legal status, administrative location and dual operational roles before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Tax administration - PAN, faceless, AIS, TDS/TCS, Charter

accepted.s: The Income Tax Department is organised into how many regions, as specified in the current administrative structure?
accepted.x: The Income Tax Department has 18 regions.
accepted.tq: Test the exact administrative count with closely spaced numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Tax administration - PAN, faceless, AIS, TDS/TCS, Charter

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Section)
A. Section 115BAA
B. Section 115BAB

List-II (Provision)
1. Existing domestic companies foregoing exemptions
2. New manufacturing companies incorporated after 1 October 2019
3. Foreign companies with permanent establishments
4. Individual taxpayers opting for a new personal tax regime

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Section 115BAA applies to existing domestic companies foregoing exemptions, while Section 115BAB applies to new manufacturing companies incorporated after 1 October 2019.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure section-to-company pairing and eliminate codes containing the wrong taxpayer category.

accepted.s: The concessional corporate tax rate under Section 115BAA for existing domestic companies foregoing exemptions is:
accepted.x: Section 115BAA provides a 22 per cent rate, with the effective rate being approximately 25.17 per cent after applicable surcharge and cess.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the statutory concessional rate from the approximate effective rate.

accepted.s: New manufacturing companies incorporated after 1 October 2019 could avail themselves of which rate under Section 115BAB?
accepted.x: Section 115BAB provides a 15 per cent corporate tax rate for eligible new manufacturing companies incorporated after 1 October 2019; the effective rate is approximately 17.01 per cent.
accepted.tq: Link the eligibility condition with the statutory rate and avoid confusing it with the effective rate.

accepted.s: The 2019 corporate tax cuts introducing Sections 115BAA and 115BAB were announced through the:
o: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act
accepted.x: The corporate tax cuts were announced in September 2019 through the Taxation Laws (Amendment) Ordinance.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct legal instrument and distinguish an ordinance from an Act, rules or commission report.

accepted.s: The 2019 corporate tax reduction was described in the Economic Survey 2025-26 as the:
accepted.x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 described the 2019 corporate tax reduction as the first pillar of tax reform, followed by personal income-tax reform and GST 2.0.
accepted.tq: Use the exact ordinal description and avoid reversing the sequence of reform pillars.

accepted.s: Which event is associated with the Income Tax Act of 1922?
o: Creation of the CBDT under the 1963 Act
Creation of the Income Tax Department
accepted.x: The Income Tax Act, 1922 created the Income Tax Department.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the historical institutional milestone from later administrative and GST reforms.

accepted.s: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) was introduced in India from:
accepted.x: STT has been levied in India from 1 October 2004.
accepted.tq: Use the exact commencement date and reject dates associated with other major tax reforms.

accepted.s: As reported up to 10 August 2026, net direct taxes had reached approximately:
accepted.x: Net direct taxes stood at approximately ₹8.11 lakh crore, showing growth of 23.09 per cent up to 10 August 2026.
accepted.tq: Check both components of the numerical claim—the absolute amount and the growth percentage.

accepted.s: Under the Budget 2026-27 changes, STT on futures and options was raised respectively to:
accepted.x: STT on futures was raised to 0.05 per cent and on options to 0.15 per cent.
accepted.tq: Preserve the order of the two financial instruments while matching their revised rates.

accepted.s: The growth in personal income tax (PIT) during 2025-26 was reported to be approximately:
accepted.x: PIT growth during 2025-26 was reported at only 0.037 per cent.
accepted.tq: Pay attention to the decimal placement in a very small percentage rather than converting it into a larger rounded figure.

accepted.s: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance that sought data on the impact of the Income-tax Act, 2025 was chaired by:
accepted.x: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance was chaired by Bhartruhari Mahtab and sought data on the Act’s impact on collections, assessees and litigation.
accepted.tq: Match the committee-related action with its chairperson rather than with officials associated with other tax reforms.

accepted.s: The principal policy rationale behind simplifying tax provisions and lowering tax rates is to promote:
o: Reduction of all indirect taxes to zero
accepted.x: Simplification and lower rates are intended to widen the tax base and encourage voluntary compliance.
accepted.tq: Translate the stated reform objective into its likely policy outcome instead of selecting an extreme consequence.

accepted.s: Which of the following is identified as a criticism in the debate on India’s tax regime?
o: Enforcement has been described as punitive, and retrospective taxation has been said to hurt investor confidence.
Tax administration has been criticised for having no enforcement powers at all.
The regime has been criticised solely for abolishing all corporate taxation.
Lower tax rates have been criticised for eliminating voluntary compliance.
accepted.x: Critics have described enforcement as punitive, while retrospective taxation has been criticised for damaging investor confidence.
accepted.tq: Find the option that combines the two stated criticisms without adding an absolute or unrelated claim.
